text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The new emergency number 112 did not function properly when the alarm was sounded when the Indonesian ambassador to Sweden's house was burning on Thursday. Authorities answered the call after 20 minutes.

- The building of housing by local authorities in Stockholm is almost at a standstill. Only 22 projects have been started in the first quarter of the year compared with 434 projects in the same 1996 period.

- A freeze in relationships between the Swedish government and leaders of the nation's major companies is not entirely accurate, says Bo Berggren, head of Industriforbundet, which represents larger industrial companies.
- A conflict among cleaning companies, which broke out two days ago, can result in late airplanes from Sweden and cancelled ferry routes.
- Continuous rain has led to floods in southern Sweden and some evacuations.

- Shipping company Nordstrom and Thulin will post a profit this year following two years of losses. But managing director Anders Berg says there is no geographical advantage to staying in Sweden and says he would consider moving the company overseas because of increased demands he expects from unions.

- Investor's managing director Claes Dahlback says shares in drug company Astra are no longer his favourites in light of delays in approvals from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for certain preparations of anti-ulcer drug Losec and lower-than-expected Losec sales in Europe.

- Swede Stig Ramel is resigning from the board of French mining company Eramet since the government sacked the company's managing director, Yves Rambaud. "I am resigning since they replaced a person because of political reasons," he told the newspaper.
